title: gpu-nsight-occupancy-analysis-2026-04-02
content:
Summary:

Quick Nsight Systems capture and Nsight Compute runs on A100-80GB instances to investigate low SM utilization observed in the production p99 traces for batch_size=1 inference. Goal was to reconcile timeline-level low GPU utilization with per-kernel metrics and to test whether CUDA Graphs improved occupancy or just reduced CPU overhead.

Environment/Setup:
- HW: NVIDIA A100 80GB (nvlink topology), driver 535.54, CUDA 12.2
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@main (commit a3f7d2c), optimizations: fast-attn fused kernels enabled, cuBLASLt for GEMM when available
- Workloads: 1) chat-infer-bs1-seq512 (raf-style attention), 2) batched-generate-bs8-seq256
- Tools: Nsight Systems 2026.1 (nSys), Nsight Compute 2026.1 (ncu), nvprof for quick checks
- Captures: nsys capture -o nsys-capture-bs1-2026-04-02 --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none <run>; ncu --target-processes all --set full -f report-bs1.ncu-rep <run>

High-level findings:
- Timeline: overall SM utilization across long captures: 40% (bs1) and 68% (bs8). Nsight timeline shows long gaps where GPU is idle between small, frequent kernels (many kernels <200us).
- Per-kernel: the largest time contributors are fused_attention_forward, fused_attention_backward, softmax_kernel, and kv_cache_update. softmax_kernel shows low achieved occupancy (20-35%) and low active warps (avg 24-48%). GEMM kernels (cuBLASLt) have high utilization but short execution times for bs1.
- Memory: L2 hit rate for attention kernels ~62-74%; global DRAM throughput capped at ~50-60% of peak with occasional spikes. Some kernels are memory-bound for long sequence lengths.
- CUDA Graphs: enabling CUDA Graphs reduced CPU-side launch overhead (observed ~18% reduction in host time per request) and improved median latency by ~12ms for bs1. However, CUDA Graphs did not materially increase achieved SM occupancy for attention kernels — occupancy remained low because individual kernel parallelism is limited by input-shaped dimensions (seq_len and head dims).

Detailed notes and evidence:
1) Timeline behavior (nsys):
- Many kernels are short-lived (~20-500us) with gaps of idle time between them. This fragmentation prevents the GPU from sustaining high average SM utilization. See capture file: nsys-capture-bs1-2026-04-02.qdrep (linked in run artifacts).
- Kernel launch serialization: NVTX spans show CPU-side serialization due to mutex in KV cache manager (lock held while preparing small device-side launches). This adds ~150-400us between launches in some hotspots.

2) Kernel-level metrics (ncu reports):
- fused_attention_forward:
  - Elapsed: ~12.3ms (bs1, seq512)
  - Achieved occupancy: 34%
  - SM Efficiency: 58%
  - Registers per thread: 64 (limiting blocks per SM)
- softmax_kernel:
  - Elapsed: ~1.6ms
  - Achieved occupancy: 22%
  - Memory throughput: low, L2 hit ~68%
- cuBLASLt_gemm (key GEMM):
  - Short, high throughput when used; occupancy >75% but elapsed << attention kernels for bs1.

Interpretation:
- Low occupancy is primarily a function of problem size (batch=1, sequence length moderate) and register usage in attention kernels. High register pressure (64 regs/thread) reduces active warps per SM. Combined with small block counts for attention kernels, we cannot fill SMs effectively.
- Fragmentation from many small kernels and CPU-side serial work (KV cache locks) causes idle gaps — even if individual kernels are efficient, aggregated utilization drops.
- Memory-bound behavior seen in softmax and KV update kernels suggests potential for optimizing L2 reuse (fuse ops, change layout) or increase per-thread work to amortize memory latency.
- CUDA Graphs help CPU overhead but do not change per-kernel occupancy unless kernels are restructured to increase parallelism per launch.

Quick wins / recommendations:
- Short term (low-effort experiments):
  - Increase batch size when possible (bs=1->bs=2/4) for production to aggregate work and improve occupancy; test tail-latency impact. Owner: Samir.
  - Reduce register usage in fused_attention kernels: try compiling with -maxrregcount=48 for an experiment build and measure occupancy change. Owner: Diego.
  - Audit KV cache locking: move to lock-free or coarser-grained batch-level lock to reduce CPU serialization. Owner: Rachel.

- Medium term (engineer effort):
  - Kernel fusion: combine softmax + scale + add operations to reduce intermediate memops and kernel launches. This should improve L2 reuse and reduce gaps. (PR idea: serving-runtime#812). Owner: Aisha + Diego.
  - Persistent kernel or tiled attention: implement a persistent attention kernel that processes multiple heads/rows per thread block to increase active warps for small batches. Prototype and run ncu.
  - Revisit use of cuBLASLt workspace to prefer larger GEMM shapes when possible; consider padding sequences to next multiple that increases GEMM efficiency (cost vs latency tradeoff).

- Long term / research:
  - Auto-fuser: build compiler pass that fuses small attention sub-ops at JIT level, guided by profiling heatmaps.
  - Investigate mixed-precision kernels and quantization that enable denser computation per thread and reduce memory bandwidth.

Concrete next experiments (prioritized):
1) Compile fused_attention with -maxrregcount=48 and capture ncu + nsys for bs1 seq512; compare occupancy and elapsed. (Diego) — target by 2026-04-09.
2) Small change: remove KV mutex or change to per-request lock in dev branch and capture timeline to measure reduction in host-side inter-kernel idle time. (Rachel) — target by 2026-04-07.
3) Prototype softmax+scale fusion in a dev kernel and benchmark for seq=512, bs=1/4. Measure L2 hit rate and change in elapsed time. (Aisha) — spike 2 weeks.

Run commands & artifacts:
- nsys: nsys profile --output nsys-capture-bs1-2026-04-02 --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none <binary args>
- ncu: ncu --target-processes all --set full -o ncu-bs1-report ./serving-runtime-bench --profile-params
- Captures saved: s3://redwood-internal/profiling/2026/04/nsys-capture-bs1-2026-04-02.qdrep, s3://redwood-internal/profiling/2026/04/ncu-bs1-report.ncu-rep

Notes / hypotheses to validate:
- Hypothesis A: Reducing register pressure by ~25% will increase blocks/SM and occupancy by ~20–35% for attention kernels, reducing elapsed time by ~10–18% for those kernels.
- Hypothesis B: Lock-free KV cache reduces CPU serialization and will recover ~10–20% total SM utilization in bs1 traces.

References:
- Related captures: gpu-nsight-occupancy-analysis-2026-03-29.json (previous run, similar patterns).
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/GPU+Profiling+Runbook
- Jira: INF-2345 (KV cache perf), INF-2370 (attention kernel refactor)

Action items (owners):
- Diego: -maxrregcount experiment + ncu capture (due 2026-04-09)
- Rachel: KV cache lock audit + timeline capture (due 2026-04-07)
- Aisha: prototype softmax fusion; coordinate with Diego (2-week spike)
- Samir: run bs=2/4 production-like test to quantify tail-latency cost vs occupancy win (due 2026-04-08)

Appendix (quick raw outputs):
- Overall SM utilization (nsys summary): bs1=40.2%, bs8=68.4%
- Average kernel duration distribution (bs1): <1ms: 43% of kernels, 1-5ms: 36%, >5ms: 21%
- Top 10 kernels by time share: fused_attention_forward (31%), fused_attention_backward (18%), kv_cache_update (12%), cuBLASLt_gemm (9%), softmax_kernel (6%), residual_add (4%), layernorm_fwd (3%), gelu (2%), dropout (1%), other (14%)

If reviewers want, I can attach exported screenshots from Nsight timeline and the full ncu .ncu-rep and nsys .qdrep archives to the linked S3 artifacts.

Unresolved questions:
- Is there any infra-level queuing (container scheduling, cgroup cpu throttling) causing additional host-side delays? We should check host CPU steal% and cgroup quotas on the test instances.
- For CUDA Graphs: there may be a mode that replays multiple sequences with fused kernels that could increase GPU-side parallelism — need to evaluate combined graph shapes.

-- Aisha
